name: triad

attributes.attribute: a Welsh and Irish literary form
lists three examples of a quality, person, or place
mystic power of the number three aided memory

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The triad is a literary form shared by the Welsh and the Irish. Because the number three held mystic weight to the Celts, and to ease memory, poets and other bards made many short verses. Each verse sets out three examples of a quality, a person, or a place. The list of Welsh triads names the three splendid women of King Arthur's court. The form also sets down the three sorrows of Ireland. Scholars read the triads for the myth material they hold.

okr.objective: Record the Welsh and Irish literary form the triad.
